v: Some say “The Pilgrim’s Progress” isn’t mine,
insinuating that I’d like to shine
in name and fame by what is someone other’s,
like those grown rich by robbing their own brothers;
or that I’m so in love with being sire
I’ll claim another’s child; or, if need require,
I’ll tell a lie in print to win applause.
I scorn it: John such a dirt-heap never was
since God converted him. Let this suffice
to show I own my “Pilgrim” at any price.
It came from my own heart, so to my head,
and down into my fingers trickling sped;
then to my pen, from which immediately
I dribbled it on paper daintily.
Manner and matter too were all my own,
nor was it to a single mortal known
till I had done it; nor did any then,
by books, by wits, by tongues, or hand, or pen,
add five words to it, or write half a line
of it: the whole, and every bit, is mine.
And as for THIS, which now your eye is on,
the matter in this manner came from none
but the same heart, and head, and fingers, and pen,
as did the other. Witness, all good men;
for none in all the world, unless he lie,
can say that this is his, but only I.
I write this not from any ostentation,
nor seeking from men praise and commendation;
I do it to forestall such base surmise
as tempts some men my name to scandalize.
Witness my name. Rearrange it, and see:
The letters make—‘Nu hony in a B.’
